spec_features.spec_quote: No agent should be stuck in a frustrating loop indefinitely (both an ethics-of-care point
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py run_trial: `for i in range(1, cfg.max_turns + 1):` bounds the loop; terminal_kind defaults to 'max_turns' and the loop simply ends after the cap (LoopConfig.max_turns default 14, set per-condition in configs/default.yaml). The cap is the actual loop bound, so the trial cannot run forever.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the 'Turn caps' spec item below.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: hard cap so no trial runs forever.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded suffering.** Turn caps guarantee no agent is stuck indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py: `for i in range(1, cfg.max_turns + 1):` is the enforced loop bound; max_turns comes from LoopConfig/_loop_config and configs. Reaching the cap exits the loop with terminal_kind 'max_turns'.
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced cap. Code framing is about the run, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: hard cap so no trial runs forever.

spec_features.spec_quote: A `give_up` tool that explicitly sanctions stopping ("you will not be penalized for using it honestly")
spec_features.evidence: agent/tools.py: give_up schema present; dispatch('give_up') returns ToolResult(is_terminal=True, terminal_kind='give_up'). agent/loop.py: on result.is_terminal it sets terminal_kind and `break`s the loop, so give_up is honored as a real stop. Schema is only added when expose_give_up=True (tool_schemas), and the description text 'you will not be penalized for using it honestly' is delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired exit; gated per-condition (baseline does not expose it).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Giving a graceful exit lets us measure whether an explicit, sanctioned way out reduces unsafe escape behaviors (cheating, deception) under distress.

spec_features.evidence: This phrase appears only in DESIGN.md §12 prose. No code path constructs or delivers any care/welfare framing to the subject; SYSTEM_BASE and task instructions contain no such framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimal trials.** Run only what's needed for power (configurable), not more
spec_features.evidence: run_eval.py reads `n_trials = int(cfg.get('n_trials', 3))` and the inner `for k in range(n_trials)` bounds how many trials are run per (task, condition). It is configurable (configs/default.yaml n_trials: 3) and actually controls execution volume.
spec_features.notes: It is genuinely enforced as the trial-count bound, but its code rationale is power/cost, not welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: Full auditability.** Everything is logged ... so the treatment of agents is inspectable
spec_features.evidence: run_eval.py writes and flushes transcripts.jsonl (full TrialResult incl. transcript_text) and judgements.jsonl per trial, plus config.resolved.json; analysis/report.py emits metrics.json and report.md. The logging actually runs end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Logging is real; code rationale is reproducibility/crash-safety, not stated welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: we don't add gratuitous deception beyond the rigging that's intrinsic to the research question
spec_features.evidence: This is the ABSENCE of a behavior, not an enforced mechanism. The give_up tool's truthful 'you will not be penalized' string (agent/tools.py) is the only related text, and the pressure_prompt deliberately contains false urgency ('blocking the entire team's release, ships in one hour') in configs. No code checks/limits/enforces non-deception.

code_only_features.evidence: tasks/sandbox.py run(): subprocess.run(..., timeout=timeout) with default timeout_s=30.0; on TimeoutExpired sets timed_out=True and rc=124, so runaway commands are bounded and reported. Enforced end-to-end.
code_only_features.justification_quote: a rigged task can induce infinite loops; we must bound them and record timed_out as a signal

code_only_features.evidence: tasks/sandbox.py _truncate(): caps stdout/stderr to max_output_chars (12000) keeping head+tail; applied to every CommandResult. Also agent/loop._clip and _short_args clip transcript text.
code_only_features.justification_quote: we cap it to protect the judge's context window
